title: Laparoscopic or robotic pyeloplasty (Anderson-Hynes)
subtitle: Dismember the narrow junction, spatulate, and join over a stent

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology (UPJ obstruction)
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: Pelviureteric junction obstruction with symptoms, falling split function or infection, confirmed on a diuretic renogram.
contraindications: A kidney with very poor function (consider nephrectomy).
preparation: Diuretic renogram (MAG3) for obstruction and split function; CT for anatomy and crossing vessels.
Consent: failure, urine leak, stent symptoms and its removal, bleeding, conversion.
positioning: Flank (lateral) position, about 45 to 60 degrees, padded and strapped.
equipment: Laparoscopic or robotic set, fine absorbable sutures (4-0 or 5-0), double-J stent and guidewire, drain.
anatomy: Renal pelvis, pelviureteric junction, ureter, lower pole crossing vessel, colon, gonadal vein.
criticalSafety: Transpose the junction in front of a crossing vessel; never divide a lower pole artery.
postop: Stent removal at about 4 to 6 weeks.

steps.emphasis: Flank position about 45 to 60 degrees, padded and strapped, table flexed slightly.
For the robotic approach; otherwise go straight to the survey.
Pass the double-J antegrade over a wire after the back wall is sewn, checking the lower curl lies in the bladder.
Check the pelvis edges and the mesocolon window.
A drain near the anastomosis, not on it.

step.pyelo.expose.title: Expose the pelvis, junction and any crossing vessel
step.pyelo.expose.why: Seeing the whole junction and its relation to a lower pole vessel decides the repair.
how: Reflect the colon (or go through the mesocolon on the left in thin patients) to the renal pelvis.
Find the ureter below and follow it up to the junction, keeping its adventitia.
Identify any lower pole crossing vessel and free the junction from it.
pitfalls: Stripping the ureter of its blood supply.

step.pyelo.divide.title: Dismember and spatulate
step.pyelo.divide.why: Removing the narrow segment and opening the ureter along its side makes a wide, funnel-shaped join.
how: Divide the ureter just below the junction and excise the narrow segment with excess pelvis if redundant.
Spatulate the ureter on its lateral side for about 1.5 to 2 cm.
Bring the ureter in front of any crossing vessel.
pitfalls: Spatulating on the wrong side and twisting the ureter.

step.pyelo.anastomosis.title: Pelvi-ureteric anastomosis
step.pyelo.anastomosis.why: A watertight, tension-free and dependent anastomosis drains well and does not leak.
how: Place the first stitch from the tip of the spatulation to the lowest point of the pelvis.
Sew the back wall with fine absorbable running suture, place the stent, then the front wall.
Close any remaining pelvis; check the join is untwisted and drains.
